source: Actual local k3d/Kubernetes requests through the assembled race-instrumented stackd executable and signed AWS SDK for Go v2; not a native AWS GuardDuty capture
corrections: The installed k3d was v5.7.5; the adapter requires v5.8.3. The successful workflow used v5.8.3 with its published SHA-256 verified.
The initial detector assertion incorrectly treated foundational enabled DNS/flow settings as optional-source activation; assertions now check only the explicitly requested optional features.

Credentialless native HTTPS returned 401 with K3s defaults. The smoke temporarily enabled anonymous authentication only on its exact-owned loopback control plane, exercised namespace-scoped RBAC, revoked it, restored configuration and observed 401 again. Production authentication defaults are unchanged.
The first fixture installation found no config.yaml.d directory. The fixture now creates that directory in its exact-owned control plane before installing the unique additive drop-in.
limits: These four metadata predicates are observable subsets, not complete EKS Protection or AWS private anomaly-model equivalence.
The security projection does not retain request/response bodies; pod-spec, RBAC policy analysis and threat telemetry remain missing.
CloudWatch logging remained disabled. No CreateSampleFindings call or fabricated native webhook event was used.
Successful cleanup removed the owned cluster, detector, IAM role/policy, subnets/VPC, controller and temporary runtime/database directory.
scope: Actual local EKS/k3d audit operations; no sample findings or injected webhook events
